newsitem.title: USA: US thrifts future earnings to offset charge - ACB.
newsitem.headline: US thrifts future earnings to offset charge - ACB.

text.p: Future earnings in the thrift industry will offset the hit taken from a one-time special charge to boost the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF), America's Community Bankers said Friday.

"This payment is expected to reduce industry net income by about 28 percent after taxes," the thrift trade group said. "Future earnings will more than offset the negative impact on third quarter earnings...," ACB said.
Reduced industry premiums for the SAIF, which insures deposits at thrifts, will make up for the one-time special assessment, ACB said.
Under recently passed legislation, the thrift industry must pay a one-time charge totaling $4.5 billion to recapitalize the SAIF.

After the fund reaches its mandated level, thrift deposit insurance premiums will drop to 6.4 cents per $100 of insured deposits from an average of 23.4 cents, starting January 1, 1997, ACB said. Those premiums will be reduced even more later on, the group said.
"Reduced third quarter earnings for SAIF-insured institutions should not be taken as a sign of structural weakness for the industry," ACB said.
Return on assets will be about 0.73 percent for 1996, ACB said. That compared with 1.01 percent that would have been achieved without the special assessment and 0.77 percent in 1995, the group said.
